=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28285-28360 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Gate D does not receive consumer-configured `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK` and `AUTO_MERGE_WAIT_WORKFLOWS`, so it may not enforce the configured required check or its workflow binding.
  WHY: The helper reads these settings from the process environment, but the poller does not map them in; severity is disputed because Sonnet says this is not a regression and calls for qualifying the documentation, while Gemini and OpenAI rate the runtime risk major.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28048-54 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Gate C treats commit author or committer name and email as proof that the pipeline created the commit.
  WHY: A same-repository contributor can create a matching `[ai-autofix]` or `[judge-fix]` commit with the hard-coded identity, causing the sweep to treat it as productive and use its timestamp.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28232-53 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: Gate B does not bind the selected pipeline-authored editor summary to `N_HEAD_SHA`.
  WHY: A contributor can push a new commit after a valid summary, and Gate D may approve that new head using the old summary if its CI passes.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28160-28176 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: When the snapshot lacks `headRefOid` but the live PR read has a valid SHA, the mismatch is logged as “head moved during sweep.”
  WHY: The fail-closed skip is correct, but the misleading diagnostic attributes it to head movement rather than missing snapshot data.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28114-28122 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The fingerprint-cap block makes a redundant `/user` request instead of reusing the trusted login already resolved for the PR.
  WHY: Each PR reaching the cap block can incur one unnecessary API call.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28011-28019 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `N_COMMENTS_JSON` is read before `unblock_trusted_login` verifies the pipeline login.
  WHY: A same-repository PR skipped because the login probe fails still incurs one comments API request.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28300-28313 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The named-CI-check requirement comes from `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK`, which defaults to `lint` only for this repository's bases. The poller does not forward a consumer's repository variable. In a consumer repo that has set it, Gate D resolves the check to `none` and does not require the named check. The changelog and agents fragment say Gate D "uses the same required-checks rule as review auto-merge", which overstates this for such consumers.
  WHY: Required check-runs are still enforced through the shared `_pr_checks_completed` filter, and an empty listing fails closed in the poller. This is not a regression, because the old Gate D required no named check at all. It would be fully closed only by wiring the variable through `orchestrate_poll.yml`, which is outside the plan's `files_touched`. The in-scope correction is to qualify the wording in the changelog and agents fragments.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28285-28360 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The poller does not pass or default the repository-configured variables `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK` and `AUTO_MERGE_WAIT_WORKFLOWS` to the `_pr_wait_for_required_checks` call.
  WHY: Consumer repositories that have configured a custom required CI check will have their Gate D enforce the repository default (lint) instead of their configured requirement, leading to potentially merging PRs that fail custom CI checks.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28160-28173 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: When the snapshot data lacks `headRefOid` (empty), but the live PR read succeeds with a valid SHA, the log reports "head moved during sweep" even though the head did not move.
  WHY: Misleading diagnostic information complicates troubleshooting for operators, as it falsely attributes a safe, fail-closed skip to branch activity.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28169-28173 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: When the snapshot lacks `headRefOid` (`N_HEAD_OID` is empty) but the live PR read has a valid 40-hex `N_HEAD_SHA`, the `[ "${N_HEAD_SHA}" != "${N_HEAD_OID}" ]` comparison fires and the log says "head moved during sweep (unknown -> …)". The snapshot never had the field, so the message misattributes the skip.
  WHY: Same-repo PR with a partial `gh pr list --json` response gets routed as a "head moved" event; operator/audit follow-up chases a non-event. Behaviour is still correct (skip), so this is not a security regression.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28011-28019 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: `N_COMMENTS_JSON` is read before `unblock_trusted_login >/dev/null`. A same-repo PR whose pipeline-login probe fails (no PAT, expired token, GH_PAT not exporting a verified login) costs one `/issues/N/comments` page before being skipped.
  WHY: One extra paginated REST call only on the noop-retry-cap path; not a hot path. Security outcome is unaffected because the trusted-login filter still gates the merge. The fork-exclusion earlier in the loop already avoids this for fork PRs.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28048-54 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Gate C treats the commit’s author or committer name/email as proof that the pipeline created it. Those fields are supplied by whoever creates the commit and are not authenticated by this comparison.
  WHY: A same-repository contributor can create an `[ai-autofix]` or `[judge-fix]` commit with the hard-coded `codex-bot` name and email. The sweep then treats that commit as productive and uses its timestamp to calculate the trusted-warning count. This does not verify the commit’s provenance as required.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28232-53 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Gate B selects the latest pipeline-authored editor summary and validates its arithmetic, but does not bind that summary to `N_HEAD_SHA`.
  WHY: After a valid summary is posted, a contributor can push another commit to the PR. If that new head’s CI passes before a new review summary is posted, the sweep can validate the old summary and Gate D can approve the new head. The head-snapshot comparison and `--match-head-commit` bind the PR read and merge to the new head, not the summary’s audit.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28307-13; .github/workflows/orchestrate_poll.yml:1048-77 | severity=high | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: Gate D’s wait helper reads `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK` and `AUTO_MERGE_WAIT_WORKFLOWS` from the process environment, but the poller step does not map either repository variable into its environment.
  WHY: In consumer repositories, the helper defaults the named check to `none`. A configured `AUTO_MERGE_REQUIRED_CI_CHECK` therefore is not enforced by this force-merge path; if the configured check is produced by a workflow other than the helper’s default `CI`, the workflow-to-check binding is also unavailable. The review auto-merge path explicitly exports these settings, so this path does not apply the same configured check policy.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28175-28176 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: When the snapshot lacks `headRefOid` (so `N_HEAD_OID` is empty) but the live PR read returns a valid 40-char `N_HEAD_SHA`, the condition `[ "${N_HEAD_SHA}" != "${N_HEAD_OID}" ]` is true and the log reads "head moved during sweep (unknown -> <sha>)". The snapshot data was missing, not the head moving.
  WHY: The fail-closed skip is correct, but the diagnostic message attributes the skip to head movement rather than missing snapshot data. An operator investigating from logs would chase the wrong cause.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:28114-28122 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The fingerprint-cap block resolves `NOOP_CAP_TRUSTED_LOGIN` via a separate `gh_retry _safe_gh_jq "user"` call, even though `N_TRUSTED_LOGIN` was already resolved at line 28017 by `unblock_trusted_login` (which caches the result in `UNBLOCK_TRUSTED_LOGIN`). The cap block only needs the lowercased form for the `grep -Fxq` comparison against the `ascii_downcase` author list.
  WHY: One redundant `GET /user` API call per PR that reaches the cap block when `NOOP_CAP_TRUSTED_LOGIN_STATE` is unset. The fix is to set `NOOP_CAP_TRUSTED_LOGIN="${N_TRUSTED_LOGIN,,}"` and `NOOP_CAP_TRUSTED_LOGIN_STATE="ok"` (or "failed" if `N_TRUSTED_LOGIN` is empty, but that case is already handled by the fail-closed skip at line 28019-28022). This is a §14 API-call-budget concern.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
